verses.text: Wake up, wake up, Zion! Clothe yourself with strength. Put on your beautiful clothes, Jerusalem, the holy city. For those who are uncircumcised and unclean will never enter you again.
Shake off the dust! Get up and sit on your throne, Jerusalem! Take off the chains from your neck, captive daughter of Zion!
For this is what the LORD says: "You were sold for nothing, and you will be rescued without money."
For this is what the Lord GOD says: "Long ago my people went down to live in Egypt. Later Assyria treated them cruelly for no reason.
And now, what do I have here?" says the LORD. "My people have been taken away for nothing. Those who rule over them mock them," says the LORD. "And all day long my name is insulted.
So my people will know my name. On that day they will know that I am the one who speaks. Yes, it is I."
How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of those who bring good news, who announce peace, who bring good news of good things, who announce salvation, who say to Zion, "Your God is King!"
Listen! Your watchmen raise their voices. Together they shout for joy. For with their own eyes they will see the LORD return to Zion.
Burst into songs of joy together, you ruins of Jerusalem! For the LORD has comforted his people. He has rescued Jerusalem.
The LORD will show his holy power in front of all the nations. All the ends of the earth will see the salvation of our God.
Leave, leave, go out from there! Do not touch anything unclean! Come out from it and make yourselves pure, you who carry the holy objects of the LORD's house.
But you will not leave in a hurry. You will not go running away. For the LORD will go ahead of you, and the God of Israel will guard you from behind.
Look, my servant will act wisely. He will be raised and lifted up and highly honored.
Many people were shocked when they saw him. His face was so damaged that he hardly looked human. His body was so disfigured that he no longer looked like a man.
But he will sprinkle many nations, and kings will shut their mouths because of him. For they will see what they had never been told, and they will understand what they had never heard.
